commitResults.messageTitle: Parse deadline and event dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously dates were stored as free-text strings, so Noms could not
reason about them. Store them as java.time.LocalDate instead: accept
ISO yyyy-mm-dd input and display as MMM dd yyyy.

Add a DateUtil helper for parsing and formatting, and an
InvalidDateException so unparseable dates get a friendly Noms message
instead of a crash. Add an "on <date>" command that lists deadlines
falling on a date and events spanning it.

Save files now store dates in ISO form so they round-trip exactly;
old free-text dates in an existing save file will be skipped on load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
Extract Ui class for console interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
Move all reading of user input and printing of responses out of the
Noms main class into a dedicated Ui class, the first step of the
A-MoreOOP extraction toward separate Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList
responsibilities.

Ui now owns the Scanner, the horizontal divider constant (previously a
repeated string literal), the welcome banner, and one intention-revealing
method per response (showTaskAdded, showTaskMarked, showTasksOn, etc.).
Noms calls these instead of inlining System.out.println, so the main
loop reads as command handling rather than formatting.

To keep Ui free of task-selection logic, the old printTasksOn helper is
split into parseOnDate/tasksOn (which compute the matching tasks) and
Ui.showTasksOn (which only prints them). Behavior and output are
unchanged: all 18 console UI regression cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class for task-list operations
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the task collection and the operations on it out of Noms into a
dedicated TaskList class, the second step of the A-MoreOOP extraction.

Noms previously held a raw List<Task> and manipulated it inline with
add/get/remove and an ad-hoc static tasksOn helper. TaskList now owns
that list and exposes intention-revealing operations (add, delete, get,
size, tasksOn), so the main loop expresses what it wants done rather than
how the list is stored. Noms constructs the list at startup as
new TaskList(storage.load()), matching the target design.

Storage still reads and writes a plain List<Task>; TaskList.asList()
bridges to it at the save/load boundary, so Storage is untouched this
step. Behavior and output are unchanged: all 18 console UI regression
cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class for command interpretation
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the code that makes sense of user commands out of Noms into a
dedicated Parser class, the third step of the A-MoreOOP extraction.

Parser now owns getCommandType, parseTask, parseTaskNumber, parseOnDate,
and the todo/deadline/event format strings those methods reference. Noms
calls Parser.parseX(...) and is left with just the dispatch loop wiring
Ui, Storage, and TaskList together, dropping from ~236 to ~101 lines.

The parsing methods are static because they depend only on their input
string; grouping the command-format knowledge in one class keeps it out
of the main loop. Behavior and output are unchanged: all 18 console UI
regression cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn Noms into an instantiable driver with run()
commitResults.messageBody:
Convert Noms from a single static main into a proper object, the final
step of the A-MoreOOP extraction.

Noms now holds ui, storage, and tasks as instance fields. A constructor
wires them up and loads the saved tasks (falling back to an empty list on
a read error), and a run() method holds the command loop. main is reduced
to `new Noms(...).run()`, matching the target design. saveTasks is now an
instance method that reads the fields directly instead of receiving them
as parameters.

The constructor takes the save directory and file name separately rather
than a single path string, because Storage already models the location
that way for cross-platform safety; threading the two values through is
consistent with that existing design. The one behavioral nuance is that a
load error (a rare, untested path) is now reported before the welcome
banner rather than after; all 18 console UI regression cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce Command hierarchy for the dispatch loop
commitResults.messageBody:
Apply the Command design pattern (the A-MoreOOP stretch goal): replace the
long if/else-if chain in Noms.run with one Command subclass per command.

An abstract Command declares execute(tasks, ui, storage) and isExit(), and
provides a shared save() helper so every task-changing command persists in
the same way. AddCommand, ListCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand,
DeleteCommand, OnCommand, and ExitCommand each carry out one command.
Parser.parse now maps a command line to the right Command: parsing that
needs no task list (descriptions, dates) happens up front, while task-number
range checks that depend on the current list size stay in execute.

Noms.run becomes the pattern's polymorphic loop
(parse -> execute -> isExit), so adding a future command means adding a
class and a switch case, not editing the loop.

Divergence from the stretch-goal snippet: that snippet shows ui.showLine()
before and after each command, but this project's Ui methods already print
their own trailing divider (from the earlier Ui extraction), so calling
showLine() as well would double every divider. The divider responsibility
is left in Ui to keep console output byte-for-byte unchanged; all 18
console UI regression cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Route save-file warnings through Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
Keep all console output in one place: Storage no longer prints to
System.out when it skips an unparseable save-file line.

Storage.load now records each skipped line and exposes them via
getSkippedLines(); the Noms constructor reports them through
ui.showError after loading. This removes the last System.out call
outside Ui, so Storage is free of any user-interface concern.

The warning's wording and format are unchanged, so console output is
identical. Add TC-019 to the UI test plan to cover the corrupt-line
path (previously untested): it pre-seeds the save file with a good line,
a garbage line, and another good line, and verifies the good tasks load
while the bad line is skipped and reported. Also fix a stale reference
in the plan preamble that numbered the two-run persistence cases 18/19
instead of 17/18.

Add JUnit tests for DateUtil.parse
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce the project's first automated test class, covering the
date-parsing logic that deadline, event, and on commands rely on.

DateUtil.parse is a pure static method with a well-defined contract
(valid ISO date -> LocalDate, otherwise InvalidDateException), which
makes it a good first target for JUnit: the cases assert both the
accepted format and the main rejection paths (impossible calendar
dates, leap day in a non-leap year, non-ISO formats, missing zero
padding, and non-date text), guarding against regressions as the
parsing code evolves.

Place the test under src/test/java/noms/util to follow the Gradle
and JUnit source-set convention, mirroring the package of the class
under test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add DateUtil.format tests to DateUtilTest
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover the class's second public method, format(LocalDate), so the whole
of DateUtil's observable behavior is now tested.

format is not a trivial getter: it renders a date through the display
pattern "MMM dd yyyy", which pads the day to two digits and abbreviates
the month using the JDK's locale data (notably "Sept" for September).
The added cases pin down a typical date, the two-digit day padding, an
end-of-year date, that four-letter September abbreviation, and a
parse-then-format round trip, so a change to the display format is
caught rather than silently altering task listings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for core parsing, task, and storage logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Extend the test suite to the highest-value methods across the codebase,
targeting the roughly half that carry complex, core, or critical logic
while leaving the thin accessors, display formatting, and console-facing
orchestration untested for now.

Covered:
- Parser: command recognition, task parsing for all three task types,
  task-number validation (including the integer-overflow path), on-date
  extraction, and top-level dispatch to the right Command.
- Task: the save-file escape/unescape rules and each type's on-disk
  format, which guard against silent save-file corruption.
- Deadline and Event: the occursOn date checks, exercising the inclusive
  range boundaries an event spans.
- TaskList: the tasksOn date filter, delete-and-renumber, and the
  defensive copying done by the constructor and asList.
- Storage: round-tripping every task type, tolerating a corrupted line,
  and preserving descriptions containing the format's own | and \
  characters, using a JUnit temporary directory so no real save file is
  touched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Document JUnit test coverage target in AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Record the ~50% highest-value-method coverage target so the expectation
is captured for future AI-assisted work, alongside the existing console
UI regression rule.

State that JUnit tests must be updated after each code change to keep the
target met: add tests for new high-value methods, update tests the change
affects, and run ./gradlew test (still run it for lower-value or test-only
changes to catch regressions). Also note where tests live and how the test
path mirrors the class under test, matching the layout just added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for state-changing command execute methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Extend coverage toward the stretch goal of testing every non-trivial
public method, adding the command layer's core behavior.

Cover the execute methods that change state and persist it (add, delete,
mark, unmark) by asserting the resulting task-list state and the reloaded
save-file contents, plus their invalid-task-number error paths. Also test
ExitCommand.isExit, the one override that stops the main loop, against a
non-exit command for contrast.

Assert observable state rather than console text: the printed responses
are covered by the console UI regression plan, and asserting exact output
in JUnit would be brittle. Standard output is redirected during these
tests so the commands' prints do not clutter the test log, and a JUnit
temporary directory backs storage so no real save file is touched.

The trivial one-line delegations (ListCommand and OnCommand execute) and
the console-only Ui and Noms driver are intentionally left to the UI
regression plan rather than duplicated as brittle output assertions here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Package app as a fat JAR via shadowJar
commitResults.messageBody:
Point the application's mainClass at the actual entry point, noms.Noms
(it was still the template's seedu.duke.Duke, so the packaged JAR had a
wrong Main-Class and would not launch), and name the shadowJar output
noms.jar so the distributable file matches the product.

This lets `./gradlew shadowJar` produce build/libs/noms.jar, a
self-contained executable JAR that runs anywhere with
`java -jar "noms.jar"` for distribution via a GitHub release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add Javadoc to remaining non-private members
commitResults.messageBody:
Complete Javadoc coverage to the A-JavaDoc stretch goal: header
comments now cover every non-private class, method, and constructor,
plus the non-trivial private methods that were already documented.

Per the se-education intermediate standard, constructors count as
public methods and require headers, so this documents the previously
undocumented task constructors (ToDo, Deadline, Event) and all nine
NomsException subclass constructors, the ToDo class header, and
Noms.main(). The five command constructors that had a bare @param tag
now also carry a summary sentence, since the standard requires the
first Javadoc sentence to be a short summary.

Overrides with inherited doc (execute, isExit, toString, toFileFormat)
are left undocumented as the standard permits. Comment-only change:
no logic touched; ./gradlew test passes and UI transcript TC-001 is
byte-identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill and enforce it
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a project-specific `seedu-java-coding-standard` skill that
encodes the se-education intermediate Java conventions (naming, layout,
imports, comments/Javadoc, statements, class design) as the single
authoritative ruleset, with a self-check review checklist.

Make it the source of truth to avoid two copies drifting: trim
docs/style-guide.md to a pointer at the skill while keeping the Git
conventions there, and update AGENTS.md to mandate invoking the skill
and self-checking every Java change against its checklist.

Bring existing code into line with the standard's American-spelling
rule: replace British spellings (recognise/centralise) in Javadoc and
comments across Ui, Parser, Storage, and UnknownCommandException, and
rename the ParserTest method accordingly. These are comment/identifier
changes only, so console UI behavior is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill and enforce it
commitResults.messageBody:
Commit and branch conventions were only summarized as a few bullets in
docs/style-guide.md, with no single authoritative reference for future
commits to follow.

Introduce a project-specific `seedu-git-standard` skill that encodes the
se-education Git conventions (imperative subject, 50/72 length limits,
WHAT-and-WHY body, kebab-case branch names) as the source of truth, with
a worked example and a review checklist.

Point the two agent files at it: trim the Git section of
docs/style-guide.md to a pointer at the skill, and update the AGENTS.md
Git section to mandate invoking the skill and self-checking against its
checklist for every commit, while keeping the project-specific tag and
commit/push policy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
